title: feat(spec,plugin-audit): seal audit-class objects that declare lifecycle.seal into signed, chained checkpoints
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBUgtYDMYUKEFZYtaQrUg9Lr)_

Part of #31908

Clause-②: yes (widening) (a new optional key; its refusals bind only an object that declares it, and none does on main)
Metadata-protocol: added (`lifecycle.seal` joins the ADR-0057 lifecycle block)
Skills-docs: follow-up #32364

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：ADR-0154 的 P1b-2。spec 新增 `lifecycle.seal = { valueFields }` 及 7 条编写期拒收；plugin-audit 新增封存器（`kernel:ready` 启动，按小时窗口把审计行封进带签名、成链的检查点）和默认 Ed25519 签名器（首次签名时建密钥，并写一行 `audit_signing_key_change` 账本）；每种字段类型都有唯一规范写法或明确无规则（Q5 规则表）。
- 为什么改：这是 ADR-0154 防篡改的读取方（ADR-0049 配对：新 key 与它的读取方同 PR 落地）；P2 的 `os audit verify` 要核验的就是这里写出的检查点。
- 风险与回滚：默认没有任何对象声明 `lifecycle.seal`（`sys_audit_log` 的默认值在 P4），所以合入后封存器每轮只读注册表、什么都不写。宿主没传 `cryptoProvider` 时，声明了 seal 的对象在 error 级报告，故障持续时每小时再报一次。回滚就是整体 revert。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/sealer.ts`（窗口、迟到行、锁、S1 循环），`signer.ts`（私钥只经其封装的一半被信任），`canonical.ts` 的 `AUDIT_SEAL_TYPE_RULES`，以及 `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` 的 seal 拒收。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run src/audit-seal`（预期 5 个文件 96 个测试全绿，含一条真 SQLite 内核的集成测试），再跑 `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/data/object-lifecycle-seal.test.ts`（预期 20 个全绿）。
- 第二轮（合同评审 6779418107）：M1 与 S1 到 S6、S8 已改，逐项对照见下方 Round 2 一节；S7、S9 由席位承接。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。P4 合入前 cloud 不要给 `sys_ai_audit_log` 加封存 opt-in；运行时与 CLI 宿主尚未把 `cryptoProvider` 传给 AuditPlugin（见下方范围外发现）。

## What changes

**`@objectstack/spec`.**
- `lifecycle.seal = { valueFields: string[] }` (strict) opts an `audit`-class object into tamper evidence (ADR-0154 D10). Each refusal is a `custom` issue with its own path, and its message ends `(ADR-0154 D10)`:
  - `seal` on a class other than `audit`, at `lifecycle.seal`;
  - a `valueFields` name that is not a declared field, or is `id` or `created_at` (they order each leaf, so they enter in clear), at `lifecycle.seal.valueFields.N` (an object-level refinement, since the lifecycle block cannot see `fields`);
  - beside `seal`: `retention.onlyWhen` at `lifecycle.retention.onlyWhen`, `ttl.onlyWhen` at `lifecycle.ttl.onlyWhen`, a `ttl` whose `field` is not `created_at` at `lifecycle.ttl.field`, and rotation storage at `lifecycle.storage`.
- The seal description and `objects.mdx` say that until expiry amendments ship (P4), the retention sweeper still deletes sealed rows, which then read as missing.
- `crypto-provider.ts` (n1): the `audit_seal` reason now says the seed's handle id sits inside a signed checkpoint body and the signing key's private handle sits in the unsigned `sys_audit_signing_key.private_handle`, and nothing rewrites either holder. A re-id of the private handle leaves the key unable to sign or to vouch for its own public half.
- `audit-checkpoint.ts` (n2): `AuditCheckpointSinkEntry` lists every member a sink receives, member by member, for a checkpoint body and for each amendment kind.
- Generated by documented commands: `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx` and `authorable-surface/data.json` (`gen:schema`, `gen:docs`). The liveness ledger tracks `lifecycle` as one top-level key, so no entry changes.

**`@objectstack/plugin-audit`.**
- **The sealer** (`audit-seal/sealer.ts`, D3). Started at the end of the `kernel:ready` hook on a `DispatchLoop` from `@objectstack/core`, stopped first in `destroy()`. Each pass re-reads the registry for objects that declare `lifecycle.seal`.
  - Constants, no operator knob: `AUDIT_SEAL_WINDOW_MS` (1 h), `AUDIT_SEAL_SETTLE_MS` (10 min), `AUDIT_SEAL_LATE_HORIZON_MS` (7 days).
  - Holds the cluster lock `audit.sealer` (`waitMs: 0`, a 60 s TTL renewed per page, per window the late pass re-counts, and before each checkpoint) and records its fencing token on every checkpoint. With no `cluster` service it takes an in-process lock with its own per-process fencing counter and says so once at info (Q2 (a)). A lease that lapsed before the write stores nothing and drops the seed it sealed.
  - Late rows first: each sealed window of the last 7 days is re-counted on its own, and each whose stored count differs from what its checkpoints list is read; each unlisted row is sealed into a `late` checkpoint of its chain. A window is read by keyset paging on `(created_at, id)`, so rows the Archiver moves between pages are not skipped. Then the windows: the backlog oldest first, the archive datasource read beside the hot store (Q3 (a)), one checkpoint per organization chain and one deployment chain (`tenant_id` NULL) per window, none for an empty window, and the sealed-through watermark carried on each.
  - Each checkpoint: a fresh 32-byte seed sealed under `checkpointSeedContext` and written as a `sys_secret` row through the driver, below the hooks (ruling 3d), so the sealer never seals its own writes; the Merkle root of the window's leaves; the previous checkpoint's digest; signed under the S1 loop; refused when the chain already holds a window checkpoint at or after this window, re-read under the lease just before the insert (two sealers whose leases overlap); inserted through the engine with a system context; handed to the `audit.checkpointSink` slot when one is registered (a failing sink costs a warning).
  - **The S1 loop is pinned here:** the body is built with the key id the signer is expected to use, and when the signer answers another key id, rebuilt with that one and signed again. A signature whose key id differs from the one its bytes name is never stored; after 3 mismatches the checkpoint is not written.
  - **A secret is dropped only when no insert was attempted.** A failure before the checkpoint insert (the lease lapsed, the S1 loop gave up, the window is already sealed) drops the seed. An insert can reject after its row is stored (an afterInsert hook that throws, a lost acknowledgement), so after a rejected insert the checkpoint is re-read by `(sealed_object, chain_key, sequence)`: stored with this seed, it stands with a warning; not stored, the seed is left as an orphan for `os secret orphans`.
  - Reported at `error`, naming the consequence and the fix, and again each hour while the cause lasts (a later success clears an object's report): a sealed object with no crypto provider or no signer; an object with a column of no canonical rule, naming the column and its type, or with no `tenant_id` field (that object is not sealed, never folded into the deployment chain); a failed pass or object. A driver error is quoted by its reason only, never its SQL statement, whose values can hold a sealed secret's ciphertext.
- **The signer** (`audit-seal/signer.ts`, D6). `LocalCheckpointSigner` is the default `IAuditCheckpointSigner` when no `audit.checkpointSigner` service is registered. One deployment Ed25519 key in `sys_audit_signing_key`, created on the first signature: its private half sealed under `signingKeyContext(fingerprint)` and written to `sys_secret` through the driver, then one `audit_signing_key_change` ledger row (Q4 (a)), then the key row; a failed ledger write drops the sealed half and leaves no key. A rejected key-row insert re-reads the key by fingerprint: stored with this half, the key stands and signs; not stored, the half is left as an orphan for `os secret orphans`. A key row is trusted only through its wrapped private half: `trustedPublicKey` and `sign` open it under the key's own fingerprint and require it to derive the row's public half and fingerprint.
- **The key-change writer** (`audit-signing-key-audit.ts`, the one new writer file). `audit_signing_key_change` is a deployment-level `sys_audit_log` row by actor `svc:audit-sealer`, whose metadata holds only fingerprints (anything but 64 hex characters is refused). `sys_audit_log.action` gains the option, writer first.
- **Per-type rules** (`audit-seal/canonical.ts`, Q5 (a)). `AUDIT_SEAL_TYPE_RULES` is exhaustive over `FieldType` by `satisfies` (a new FieldType does not compile until it gets a rule or none). Rules: text, number, boolean, date, datetime, json; a multi-value text column reads as json. No rule: `password`, `secret`, `formula`, `summary`, `image`, `file`, `avatar`, `video`, `audio`. Number refuses a non-finite value, an unsafe integer, and a decimal text a double cannot carry exactly. Date (Q7 (a)) takes `YYYY-MM-DD` text, or a `Date` only at UTC midnight. JSON takes the parsed value or the text SQLite returns.
- `jcs.ts` (round-1 n2): a committed value's refusal names its members by position (`$.#0.#1`), never by name. `seed.ts` (n3, Q6 (a)): a seed or signing-key coordinate longer than `sys_secret.namespace` or `sys_secret.key` holds (read off the `SysSecret` declaration, 128) is refused before anything is encrypted or written.
- `AuditPluginOptions.cryptoProvider` composes the crypto provider. README: the registered-objects sentence names all six objects.

**`@objectstack/platform-objects`.** `sys-secret.object.ts`'s source comments name the audit sealer as the fourth producer (round-1 n5). `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` says four producers and four holder families (record n5); `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx` documents `lifecycle.seal`.

## Gate-held records (claim amendment 6776033453)

Each regenerated by its documented command on the merged tree, with no hand edit inside a generated block:
- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` and `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md`: `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`. Four new engine write sites: the key-change writer's `sys_audit_log` insert, the signer's key-row insert, the sealer's checkpoint insert, and the signer's best-effort `sys_secret` delete. Main (`aac03d948`) to this branch: write call sites 296 to 300; statically decidable 205 to 207; chosen at run time 91 to 93; against a tenancy-enabled object 198 to 200; threading a tenant context 227 to 230; options unreadable 57 to 58 (tenancy-enabled 30 to 31); decidably elevated 163 to 166; elevation a run-time fact 121 to 122. The provable no-context count stays 12, and 3 against a tenancy-enabled object. The census gate holds 23 prose figures to the census; the hand-written ones moved with it (296 to 300, 57 to 58, 69 to 70, 30 to 31, 205 to 207, 91 to 93, 163 to 166, 121 to 122).
- `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/data.md`: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:strictness-ledger`. The strict `seal` object adds one site: `data/` 168 to 169 sites, strict 99 to 100, strip unchanged at 67; `object.zod.ts` 25 to 26. The hand-written ledger needs no edit.

## Pins outside the surface (claim amendment 6777658851)

The package suites, which `dispatch-gates` does not derive, held four pins to what this slice changes:
- `plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-log-action-labels.test.ts`: the stored-values list gains `'audit_signing_key_change'` at its end, with the writer-first comment the earlier additions carry. No existing value moved.
- `plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-log-retired-actions.test.ts`: `ACTIONS_WITH_WRITERS` gains the row for `audit_signing_key_change`, naming `audit-signing-key-audit.ts` and its caller `LocalCheckpointSigner.createKey`.
- `spec/src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts`: one `omit` ledger row, type `object`, path `lifecycle`, key `seal`. Its reason: seal is written only by code-declared ledgers, nothing checks a seal before P2, and it is revisited in P2 or by the card that offers it (a `valueFields` picker is a form-face addition). `objectForm` does not offer seal in this slice.
- `platform-objects/src/apps/translations/object-lifecycle-panel-echo-decisions.test.ts`: the shape predicate finds the lifecycle composite by the schema keys the form offers, subtracting a one-entry `LIFECYCLE_FORM_OMITTED_KEYS` (`seal`). It now pins both the seven `LifecycleSchema` keys and the six offered. A form that starts offering seal matches no composite until the list drops it. The 32 lifecycle leaves and the ledger they need are unchanged.

## Round 2 (contract review 6779418107)

Commit `041fc793`. Each item, what changed, and the pin that holds it (each pin ablated, items 25 to 34 below):
- **M1.** `sealer.ts` `writeCheckpoint` and `signer.ts` `createKey` drop the secret only for a failure before the insert is attempted. After a rejected insert, the holder is re-read by its coordinate (the checkpoint by `sealed_object, chain_key, sequence`; the key by `fingerprint`) and the secret is kept if the row exists and names it; otherwise the error is rethrown and the secret is left as an orphan for `os secret orphans`. Pins: an insert that stores and then rejects, at each site.
- **S1.** Just before the insert, under the lease, a window checkpoint is refused when its chain already holds a window checkpoint at or after that window (a chain's windows are sealed oldest first, so that is the chain's window head). Pin: two sealers, the second sealing the window after the first read it and before the first wrote it; one checkpoint is stored and the first reports the refusal.
- **S2.** `readWindow` pages by keyset on `(created_at, id)`, each bound in the driver's own spelling of the last row's values. Pin: 510 rows in one window, 10 of them moved to the archive after the first page; all 510 are sealed.
- **S3.** `plans()` refuses an object declaring seal without a `tenant_id` field, reported at `error`, and never folds it into the deployment chain. Pin: one error line naming `tenant_id`, no checkpoint.
- **S4.** Reports repeat per cause once an hour while the cause lasts (`REPORT_REPEAT_MS`), and a successful pass clears an object's causes. Pin: a stalled object reports on pass 1, not on pass 2, and again after an hour. Per-chain isolation is carried to P4 by the seat.
- **S5.** `object.zod.ts` refuses `ttl.onlyWhen` beside seal, and `id` or `created_at` in `valueFields`, at authoring. Pins: the issue path of each.
- **S6.** `sealLate` drops the whole-horizon count shortcut, re-counts each window of the horizon, and renews the lease per window. Pin: one row deleted in one window and a late row added in another; the late row is sealed, and the lease is renewed at least once per window of the horizon.
- **S8.** The seal description and `objects.mdx` carry the expiry sentence.
- **The body's id/created_at sentence** is corrected under Acceptance notes.
- Not this round, carried by the seat: S7 (`row_ids` size) and S9 (host wiring).

**Existing assertions this round changes.**
- `audit-seal-sealer.test.ts`, "resumes a window a stopped pass left": `sys_secret` holds 4 rows, not 3. The unstored write's seed is now kept as an orphan (M1) where it used to be dropped.
- `audit-seal-sealer.test.ts`: the error-report block's title says "again each hour while it lasts" for "once"; its two run-twice cases still expect one line, since both passes fall inside the hour.
- `seal-store.testkit.ts`: the store double's matcher reads `$and`, `$or` and `$gt`, for the keyset bounds and the S1 re-read.

## Deferred to P2–P4

- **P2:** `os audit verify`, and the P1a record's n4 (refusing a stored amendment whose other-kind columns are not NULL).
- **P3:** the redaction amendments, and the registration of `sys_audit_amendment` with its translations.
- **P4:** the expiry amendments and `sys_audit_log`'s default `lifecycle.seal`; P4 is the slice that completes the card.
- Not in any slice yet (out-of-scope findings): a rotation verb for the signing key, and the host wiring of `cryptoProvider` in the runtime and the CLI.

## Acceptance notes

- **No object opts in.** Nothing on main declares `lifecycle.seal`, so a pass reads the registry and returns. The live test registers its own probe object.
- **`id`, `created_at` and `tenant_id` must be in the object's registered fields.** `sealedColumnSet` and the sealer's plan read only the field map the registry serves; an object whose map lacks one is reported at `error` and not sealed. An object the registry does not stamp with system fields must declare them.
- **Sealed rows still expire.** Until P4's expiry amendments, the retention sweeper deletes sealed rows, and verify will read them as missing. The seal description and `objects.mdx` say so.
- **The late-recount blind spot, as ruled.** One row deleted and one inserted in the same window leave that window's count unchanged, so that honest late row is not sealed into a `late` checkpoint. Detection is unaffected: verify reports the deleted row `missing` and the inserted one unsealed.
- **Cloud.** Until P4, cloud should not opt `sys_ai_audit_log` in. A cloud signer registered at `audit.checkpointSigner` must honour the S1 contract, and a cloud crypto provider must keep the handle id under `audit_seal`.

## Tests

- `spec/src/data/object-lifecycle-seal.test.ts` (20): seal on each of the four other classes, an undeclared `valueFields` name (one issue per name, at its index), `id` or `created_at` as a value field (at its index), `retention.onlyWhen`, `ttl.onlyWhen`, a ttl off `created_at` and rotation storage, each pinned by issue code and path and naming ADR-0154 D10; accepted beside `retention.maxAge` and a `created_at` ttl, with an empty `valueFields`, and through `ObjectSchema.create()`; a closed shape that requires `valueFields`; a lifecycle without it parses as before (control).
- `plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/audit-seal-rules.test.ts` (19): the rule table names every FieldType and nothing else; each rule in both driver spellings and its refusals; null under every rule; every value of a no-rule type refused, null included; unsealable columns listed with their types; members named by position in a committed value; the Q6 bound read off `SysSecret` and refused before anything is sealed.
- `audit-seal-signer.test.ts` (10): first signature creates the key; private half sealed under its fingerprint below the hooks; ledger row before key row; reuse; a failed ledger write drops the half; a key-row insert that stores and then rejects keeps the half, and the key signs (M1); trust only through a half that derives the row's public key, refused when re-keyed or missing; fingerprint-only metadata.
- `audit-seal-sealer.test.ts` (26): windows oldest first with no empty-window checkpoint; chaining and watermark; archive read once; keyset paging past rows moved between pages (S2); late rows before windows, each window re-counted with the lease renewed (S6), and a stopped pass resumed without a spurious late checkpoint; cluster lock and fencing token, a held lock, a lapsed lease; the in-process lock and its one info line; two sealers whose leases overlap (S1); the S1 re-sign and give-up; seeds below the hooks and never the sealed object; a checkpoint insert that stores and then rejects (M1); Q6; the sink; the error reports, including no `tenant_id` (S3) and a stalled object reported again after an hour (S4); a driver statement never echoed.
- `audit-seal-live.integration.test.ts` (5): a real kernel on SQLite (wasm), the plugin's own sealer with `cryptoProvider` and the in-process lock. Signatures verify under the key the signer vouches for; one `audit_signing_key_change` row; each root recomputed from the stored rows under the decrypted seed, and a row changed afterwards no longer matches; Q7: SQLite reads a `date` back as `YYYY-MM-DD` whichever spelling was written.
- `audit-seal-core.test.ts`: P1a's leaf and commitment cases now type their columns (an untyped column has no rule).
- `seal-store.testkit.ts`: the in-memory store, engine, context-binding crypto provider and logger doubles.

**Ablations.** Each went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the anchor hit once, the mutation landed, the named pin went red, and the file was restored to blob == HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty. Spec and plugin-audit suites read these sources directly, so no dist leg was needed. Round 2 changed `sealer.ts`, `signer.ts` and `object.zod.ts`, so items 1 to 23 were re-run on `041fc793`, with the figures below; 14 and 19 were respelled for the moved code (each write now sits in its own `try`), and 17 for `reportOnce`'s rename to `report`. Items 25 to 34 (round 2) also ran on `041fc793`. All 33 went red. Item 24 (round 1, on `f4902750`) survived and its guard is gone.

## Verification

Head `7ad755fd`. `origin/main` was merged three times with `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh`: at `842086478` (`46f7828a`; the two census files conflicted, main's side was taken, and the census was regenerated in `4b0c2440`), at `7575116cd` (`57cbdffe`, no conflict), and after round 2 at `aac03d948` (`2919a8dc`; the two census files conflicted with main's `1f3e6fdb`, main's side of both was taken, so the merge's census bytes equal main's; `cb636f40` is the unedited output of `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write` on `2919a8dc`, and `7ad755fd` moves the census page's hand-written figures only). Size against the merge base (`check-governed-merges --branch HEAD`): 54 files, +2735 −127, 2862 changed lines, under 3000 (round 1 read 2680).

On the merged head `7ad755fd`, under `os-verify-lock`: `check-tenant-audit-census` (300 sites certified, 23 prose figures held) and its `--self-test`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit` `test` (86 files, 1370/1370), `@objectstack/spec` `test` (835 files, 26628 passed, 1 skipped, 1 todo) and `test:repo` (91 files, 1556/1556), a spec build and `check:generated` (14 artefacts up to date), each exit 0.

Every run below was under `os-verify-lock`, on `041fc793` (before the third merge), with exit codes recorded before any pipe.

<details><summary>Build, gates, generated artefacts</summary>
